evidence: bare_number_card: seg1:start-end is a big number ('15.9' to '79.5' to '126', tagged '1998') inside a ring gauge, which is a number on a dial and not a demonstration of the record falling; seg2 is two bubbles that both say '8.3'.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: seg2:start, mid and end show two identical yellow bubbles, both labelled '8.3' and both captioned 'Before 2016 (1988-2013)'. The 'since 2016 ~30 s/yr' side never appears, and the kicker reads 'BEFORE 2016 (1988-2013) TOPS THE LIST' while the narration says the after-2016 rate is almost 4x faster.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The comparison machine was fed the same data row twice (the before-2016 row duplicated into the after-2016 slot), so the scene contradicts its own narration. Bubble area is also a weak way to show a rate of improvement.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Bind the second item to the post-2016 rate (~30 s/yr, labelled 'Since 2016') so the two values differ and 30 is visibly ~3.6x larger than 8.3. Better: show the rate as speed, for example two clocks or runners where the super-shoe era sheds seconds visibly faster, with Data pushing the faster one. Fix the kicker so the larger value tops the list.
